advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make run_mcp assert the wired gauge exists (fail loudly) rather than substituting a fresh empty gauge that drains instantly.
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:213: `gauge = getattr(server, _GAUGE_ATTR, None) or InFlightGauge()`
A fresh InFlightGauge always reports value 0, so drain_then_exit at line 148 (`while gauge.value > 0 ...`) returns immediately regardless of real in-flight work.

If wire_health failed to run or attach the gauge (build variation, future refactor), the bounded-drain guarantee the ADR relies on silently becomes a no-op — the retiring container exits mid-op without waiting.
advisory.finding: run_mcp silently substitutes a fresh empty InFlightGauge when the server has no wired gauge attribute, so the SIGTERM drain reads 0 and exits immediately — it cannot distinguish 'drained' from 'gauge was never wired'.
scenarios: build_server did not call wire_health (or a refactor detaches the attr) yet HTTP transport still boots
advisory.suggested_fix: Fetch the gauge that wire_health stashed and raise/log if absent instead of silently creating a new empty one, so a missing-wiring bug cannot masquerade as a clean drain.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fail (or at least warn) in instrument_certified_tools when an expected certified-tool name is absent from the tool manager instead of silently skipping it.
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:105: `if tool is None or getattr(tool, "is_async", False):`
src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:106: `continue`

CERTIFIED_TOOLS is a hardcoded frozenset (line 32) that must stay in lockstep with register_llm_tools; a rename in _mcp_llm.py makes get_tool(name) return None and the miss is silently skipped, so that tool's runs never move the gauge and the drain never waits for them.
advisory.finding: instrument_certified_tools silently skips a certified tool whose name is missing from the tool manager (get_tool returns None), so that op is never counted and shutdown never waits for it — a renamed/unregistered certified tool becomes invisible instead of an error.
scenarios: a certified tool is renamed or a build registers under a different name; CERTIFIED_TOOLS drifts from the real registry

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `proxy_http_version 1.1;` (and clear `Connection`) to the `/mcp` location so nginx proxies streaming Streamable-HTTP correctly.
evidence: `location /mcp {` ... `proxy_pass http://rebar_mcp;` ... `proxy_buffering off;` `proxy_read_timeout 3600s;` (infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template:127-136)
search_files for `proxy_http_version` in infra/nginx: (no matches)
search_files for `keepalive` in infra/nginx: (no matches)
`location /mcp {` (infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template:127)

Comment claims intent: `A PREFIX \`location /mcp\` (no trailing slash) so BOTH the bare \`/mcp\` endpoint and \`/mcp/...\` match` (infra/nginx/rebar.conf.template:122-123) — but nginx prefix matching also catches /mcpXXX, not only /mcp and /mcp/.
advisory.finding: The `/mcp` SSE/Streamable-HTTP nginx location sets `proxy_buffering off` and a long read timeout but does NOT set `proxy_http_version 1.1` (nor clear/upgrade the `Connection` header). nginx defaults to HTTP/1.0 toward upstreams, which cannot carry chunked request/response bodies and breaks long-lived streaming — the exact transport this location exists to serve.
merged_from: The edge location is declared as `location /mcp` (prefix, no trailing slash, no regex anchor), so it matches not only `/mcp` and `/mcp/...` but also sibling paths such as `/mcpanything` and `/mcp-foo`, routing them to the MCP upstream and widening the exposed surface beyond the intended endpoint.
scenarios: A Streamable-HTTP client opens an SSE stream through the /mcp edge and the connection is downgraded to HTTP/1.0, dropping keep-alive/chunked framing.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document/justify (or narrow) the 0.0.0.0 in-container bind for the MCP service, confirming no other container shares its network and the unauthenticated /health surface is acceptable.
evidence: `REBAR_MCP_HTTP_HOST: "0.0.0.0"` (infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:337)
`ports:` `- "127.0.0.1:8091:8091"` (infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:357-360)
Dockerfile default also `ENV REBAR_MCP_HTTP_HOST=0.0.0.0` (infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp)
/health is intentionally unauthenticated (src/rebar/_mcp_health.py register_health_route)
advisory.finding: REBAR_MCP_HTTP_HOST is set to 0.0.0.0 (bind all interfaces) inside the container, and the /health route is served unauthenticated on that bind. Least-privilege would prefer binding only the interface the loopback host-publish targets; the 0.0.0.0 bind means any other container/network attached to this service could reach /health and /mcp directly, relying entirely on the compose port publish being loopback-only.
scenarios: Another service/container is later attached to the same docker network and can reach 8091 (including unauthenticated /health) directly, bypassing the loopback-only host publish.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test driving a wrapped, ARGUMENT-taking certified tool through FastMCP's call_fn_with_arg_validation (not a direct .fn() call) to prove instrumentation preserves arg binding/validation.
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:86 `def _sync_wrapper(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:`
docstring claim src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:83-84 `the FastMCP tool manager calls fn via call_fn_with_arg_validation and honours the replaced attribute` — never exercised by a test
Real certified tool takes args: src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:205-210 `def review_plan(ticket_id: str, ref: str | None = None, source: str | None = None, force: bool = False)`

test_wired_server_moves_gauge... uses `def review_plan() -> str:` (no args) and calls `worker = threading.Thread(target=wrapped)` i.e. `wrapped()` directly, not through the tool manager (test_mcp_http_transport.py:418-429)
advisory.finding: No test invokes a wrapped certified tool that takes ARGUMENTS through FastMCP's call_fn_with_arg_validation path; _wrap_tool_fn replaces tool.fn with a *args/**kwargs wrapper, and both instrumentation tests use zero-arg stub bodies called directly, so a regression where the wrapper breaks argument binding/validation for the real (argument-taking) certified tools goes undetected.
scenarios: A wrapped certified tool is called with real arguments through FastMCP's tool-manager arg-validation path in production; the *args/**kwargs wrapper mishandles signature-based binding or defeats validation.
advisory.suggested_fix: Register a certified tool that takes a parameter, wire_health it, then invoke it via the tool manager's call path (call_tool / call_fn_with_arg_validation) with an argument and assert both the return value and the gauge movement.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that CALLS run_http_with_grace's installed SIGTERM handler and asserts it sets should_exit and drains the gauge (e.g. capture the handler via signal.getsignal and invoke it with an in-flight gauge + a fake/injected clock).
evidence: Production handler under test: src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:188-202 (`server.should_exit = True` then `drain_then_exit(...)`)
test only checks installation: test_mcp_http_transport.py:526 `assert signal.getsignal(signal.SIGTERM) not in (prev, signal.SIG_DFL)` — the handler is never called

Subprocess test builds its own handler `def _h(signum, frame): drain_then_exit(...)` and `signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, _h)` rather than exercising run_http_with_grace's _on_sigterm (test_mcp_http_transport.py, test_sigterm_grace_subprocess... script)
blocking.finding: The run_http_with_grace SIGTERM handler body (_on_sigterm: set should_exit, then drain the gauge via drain_then_exit) is never executed by any test; test_run_http_with_grace only asserts the handler was INSTALLED, and the subprocess test installs its own separate handler rather than the one run_http_with_grace registers, so a regression inside _on_sigterm is invisible.
scenarios: A change to _on_sigterm drops `server.should_exit = True`, drains the wrong gauge, or reorders drain vs. stop-intake — the process would fail to stop accepting connections or fail to drain, yet all tests stay green.
blocking.suggested_fix: After run_http_with_grace installs the handler, retrieve it via signal.getsignal(signal.SIGTERM), pre-load the gauge, invoke the handler, and assert the fake server's should_exit is True and the gauge was drained (with an injectable sleep/monotonic to keep it deterministic).

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify /health remains reachable without the proxy secret when the proxy auth strategy is active, or scope the ProxyAuthMiddleware wrap to exclude /health.
evidence: src/rebar/mcp_server.py:656: `mcp.streamable_http_app = _wrapped_streamable_http_app`
src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:113-114 docstring: '/health ... OUTSIDE the auth and transport-security middleware — an unauthenticated probe gets 200.'

run_http_with_grace calls `mcp.streamable_http_app()` (src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:176), which returns the ProxyAuthMiddleware-wrapped app when the proxy strategy is enabled, so /health is subject to the shared-secret check.
dropped.finding: The proxy auth strategy monkeypatches mcp.streamable_http_app to wrap the whole ASGI app in ProxyAuthMiddleware; when active, the /health custom route would then sit BEHIND that middleware, contradicting _mcp_health's documented 'unauthenticated /health probe gets 200' guarantee.
scenarios: a future/alternate deployment enables the proxy auth strategy (this compose file uses static only)
